purpose: How does a fixed string-length rule shape an elliptical garden?
meaning: An ellipse is the locus of planar points whose distances to two fixed foci add to 2 a. Here locus means the set of points satisfying that geometric rule. Put its foci on the horizontal axis at positions −c and c, with vertical coordinate zero and a>c. The semiminor axis is b=√(a²−c²), so enclosed area is A=πab. A moving point with coordinates x=a cos t and y=b sin t keeps the same total focus distance even while its two individual distances change.

definition.setting: A garden designer marks two fixed foci, each c metres from the center. A moving boundary marker must keep the total length of its two straight strings to those foci equal to 2 a metres. Change the long half-axis a or focus spacing c, then drag the point parameter t to see the same distance-sum rule at different places on the garden boundary.
definition.formal_latex: b=\sqrt{a^2-c^2},\quad x=a\cos t,\quad y=b\sin t,\quad d_1=\sqrt{(x+c)^2+y^2},\quad d_2=\sqrt{(x-c)^2+y^2},\quad d_1+d_2=2a,\quad A=\pi ab.

signature.a: Semimajor axis in metres, half the longest ellipse diameter
signature.b: Semiminor axis in metres, half the shortest ellipse diameter
signature.c: Distance from center to either focus in metres
signature.t: Ellipse boundary parameter in radians, generally not the polar angle
signature.d_1: Distance from the point to the left focus in metres
signature.d_2: Distance from the point to the right focus in metres
signature.A: Enclosed elliptical area in square metres

conditions: Semimajor axis a ranges from 3 to 5 metres, center-to-focus distance c from 0 to 2 metres, and boundary parameter t from 0 to 2π radians. Thus a>c, with a positive semiminor axis. At c=0 this family includes a circle.
definition.domain_notes: This is a nondegenerate planar ellipse with horizontal major axis. The semimajor axis is half its longest diameter, not a full diameter. The parameter t generally differs from the polar angle. The focus-distance strings are measured lengths, not ellipse perimeter; no orbit mechanics or general classification of conic sections is claimed.
